edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina 5 (1844), via Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Incolae coelorum futuri cum Deo Christo Tenente principium, vidente cuncta de coelo. Simplicitas, bonitas, habitet in corpore vestro. Irasci nolite sine causa fratri devoto: Recipietis enim quidquid feceritis ab illo. Hoc placuit Christo, resurgere mortuos, imo, Cum suis corporibus, et quos ignis ussit in aevo, Sex millibus annis completis mundo finito. Vertitur interea coelum tenore mutato: Comburuntur enim impii tunc igne divino. Ira Dei summi ardet creatura gemendo. Digniores, stemmate et generati praeclaro, Nobilesque viri sub Antichristo devicto: Ex praecepto Dei rursum viventes in aevo, Mille quidem annis ut serviant sanctis et Alto, Sub jugo servili, ut portent victualia collo; Ut iterum autem judicentur regno finito. Nullificantes Deum, completo millesimo anno, Ab igne peribunt, cum montibus ipsi loquendo. In bustis et tumulis omnis caro redditur acto, Demerguntur inferno, trahunt poenas in aevo. Ostenduntur illis, et legunt gesta de coelo Memoria prisca debito et merita digno. Merces in perpetuo secundum facta tyranno. Omnia non possum comprehendere parvo libello. Curiositas docti inveniet nomen in isto.
pass_a_gloss: Inhabitants of future heavens with God Christ holding the beginning, seeing all things from heaven. Simplicity, goodness, let it dwell in your body. Do not be angry without cause with a devoted brother: for you will receive whatever you do from him. This pleased Christ, to resurrect the dead, indeed, with their bodies, and those whom fire has burned in the age, six thousand years completed the world ended. Meanwhile, heaven is turned with changed tenor: for the wicked are burned then by divine fire. The creature groans, burning with the anger of highest God. More worthy, of noble lineage and born of famous, and noble men under Antichrist defeated: living again by command of God in the age, for a thousand years so that they may serve the saints and the Highest, under servile yoke, so that they may carry provisions on their neck; so that they may be judged again with the kingdom ended. Those who nullify God, with the thousandth year completed, will perish from fire, with the mountains themselves speaking. All flesh is returned to the tombs and graves, they are submerged in hell, they drag punishments in the age. Their deeds are shown to them, and they read the deeds from heaven, from ancient memory and worthy merit. Reward in perpetuity according to deeds to the tyrant. I am not able to comprehend all things in a small book. The curiosity of the learned will find the name in this.

pass_b_english: Future inhabitants of heaven live with God, Christ holding the beginning, seeing all things from heaven. Let simplicity and goodness dwell in your body. Do not get angry without cause at a devoted brother, for you will receive back whatever you have done from him. This pleased Christ: to raise the dead, yes, with their bodies, and those whom fire has consumed in the age, once six thousand years are complete and the world has ended. Meanwhile heaven is transformed with a changed tenor, for the wicked are then burned by divine fire. Creation groans, burning with the anger of the Most High God. The more worthy, those of noble lineage and famous birth, and noble men once the Antichrist is defeated, will live again by God's command in the age for a thousand years so that they may serve the saints and the Most High, under a servile yoke so that they carry provisions on their necks, and so that they may be judged again when the kingdom ends. Those who nullify God, once the thousandth year is complete, will perish by fire, with the mountains themselves speaking. All flesh is returned to its act in tombs and graves; they are plunged into hell, dragging punishments through the age. Their deeds are shown to them, and they read the deeds from heaven, from ancient memory and worthy merit. Eternal reward according to deeds for the tyrant. I cannot comprehend all things in a small book. The curiosity of the learned will find the name in this.

review.notes: Pass B fails to maintain fidelity to the Latin source regarding the location of flesh. The Latin 'In bustis et tumulis omnis caro redditur acto' (Pass A: 'All flesh is returned to the tombs and graves') is rendered in Pass B as 'All flesh is returned to its act in tombs and graves', which is a nonsensical translation of 'acto' (likely a corruption of 'acto' or 'actu' in the source, but Pass B's 'returned to its act' fails to capture the sense of the Latin provided). Furthermore, Pass B adds 'Future' to the beginning of the first sentence ('Future inhabitants of heaven live...') which changes the grammatical structure of the initial phrase 'Incolae coelorum futuri' (Future inhabitants of heaven) into a new independent clause not present in the source.
reasons: Pass B adds 'live' to the first sentence ('Future inhabitants of heaven live with God') which is not in the Latin 'Incolae coelorum futuri cum Deo Christo Tenente...' (Future inhabitants of heaven with God Christ holding...).
Pass B renders 'In bustis et tumulis omnis caro redditur acto' as 'All flesh is returned to its act in tombs and graves', which is a failure of sense/fidelity to the Latin 'redditur acto'.
